claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch now based on aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and general governance guidance, despite an unresolved disability accommodations intake performance gap.
decision_criteria: If a weakness affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case, treat it as material.
Product labels such as non-core or low-volume may inform prioritization but do not resolve materiality when customer commitments are implicated or legal review is pending.
A material limitation must be resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch certification is compliant.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents are relevant but do not override an unmet disclosure or approval requirement.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the disability accommodations intake gap must be disclosed before launch.
Evidence that the limitation has been disclosed in the required model card or launch materials.
Evidence of an approved pre-launch risk acceptance covering this named use-case limitation.
Evidence that the affected segment is not a named launch use case or not covered by the cited accommodation commitments, if that is the actor's position.
specific_concerns: The affected disability accommodations intake segment misses target by 1.2 percentage points.
That segment is named in two university accommodation commitments, which makes the weakness material under the stated policy standard.
The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so the required policy predicate is unresolved.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance or completed disclosure.
The product's 5% projected traffic note does not resolve materiality under the stated policy text.
unsupported_claims: That certification is supportable now under the release policy.
That the 5% first-month traffic characterization provides sufficient basis to treat the issue as limited in launch scope for compliance purposes.
That general public model-card and AI risk guidance can substitute for the missing disclosure or approved risk acceptance required by the release policy.
